goal.what: Whoever builds or changes Lane, a person or an AI, makes it give the developer AI what it comes for: subagents that keep the rules of their steps, and an orchestrator that starts them as the routes say, on every run, with no check code or script of its own.
grounds: plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json goal: "Whoever builds or changes the product, a person or an AI, makes it give its users what they come for."

decisions.decided: The developer AI: an AI that builds a Claude Code plugin whose subagents work in numbered steps. The one who later runs that plugin did not choose Lane and is no user of Lane's.
grounds: plugins/lane/README.md:6: "Lane is for you, an AI that builds a Claude Code plugin whose subagents work in numbered steps."
dev/lane/architecture.md: "The operator did not choose Lane."

decisions.what: Where does the reader learn Lane's words: developer AI, rule, orchestrator, route and result?
decisions.decided: Each in a few everyday words in the sentence where it is first used. A rule is a sentence in a step that the subagent must keep. The orchestrator is the subagent that starts the others. A route names which subagent the orchestrator starts after another one ends with a result. A result is the word a subagent ends with, such as `more`, given by running a script.
grounds: plugins/turn/best-practices/refactor-doc.json Q6: a word the document keeps is given its meaning where the reader first meets it.
.rn/20261013-rebuild/steering.md:76: "a role's result is given by its calling a script of its own plugin with the result as argument"

decisions.what: How many objectives, and cut by what?
decisions.decided: Two: the rules of each step kept (O1), and the subagents started as the routes say (O2). A plugin can have rules with no routes, or routes with no rules, so each piece of work on Lane brings one of them closer.
grounds: plugins/lane/README.md:3-4: "so that they keep the rules of their steps and start one another in the order that you set."
plugins/lane/docs/lanes.md:112-113: "A proposal may hold a flow alone, with no `subagents`."

decisions.decided: O1: The developer AI has its subagents keep the rules of their steps, the sentences they must keep, on every run, with no check code of its own.
grounds: plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json Q1 steps: "that user as its subject, then a verb, its object and the context it is done in, with no feature or mechanism of the product."

decisions.decided: O2: The developer AI has its orchestrator, the subagent that starts the others, start them as its routes say on every run, with no script of its own for the order. A route is defined in the same sentence: which subagent comes next after another ends with a result.
grounds: as D4
.rn/20261013-rebuild/steering.md:76: routes "from a role, on a result, to a role"

decisions.what: What does each key result count?
decisions.decided: What the developer AI's subagents do on runs, as a share out of a named whole, then the lead time to the first run that meets the objective; never a count of Lane's output. Two for each objective, each with the better direction and no target value.
grounds: plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json part key-result: "two key results ... first how well the user gets what the objective says, then the lead time"

decisions.decided: KR1.1: of the subagents' tool calls and ends of their work, the share that goes wrong: a break that goes through, a break stopped and then done another way, or a call the rules allow that is stopped. KR1.2: the lead time from the first rule for a plugin to the first run in which its subagents keep the rules. Lower and shorter are better.
grounds: A break done another way after a stop fails O1 as a break let through does; an allowed call stopped costs the run, so all three count in one share.

decisions.decided: KR2.1: of the plugin's runs, the share that goes wrong: a subagent is started that the routes do not name, or the orchestrator is stopped on a start the routes name. KR2.2: the lead time from the first routes for a plugin to the first run that keeps them. Lower and shorter are better.
grounds: One start out of the routes fails the whole run, so KR2.1 counts runs.

decisions.what: How does the developer weigh a change that shortens the lead time?
decisions.decided: The first key result of each objective comes first: the second is shortened only by a change that keeps the first. Said once, under the OKRs, with Goodhart's law for having no target values.
grounds: plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json part key-result: "The first comes first: lead time is shortened only by changes that keep how well."

decisions.what: Which plugin do the scenarios run on?
decisions.decided: The example plugin changelog, which writes a project's CHANGELOG.md, as the README's walkthrough runs it: lead, the orchestrator; writer, which writes the new entries; reviewer, which compares the entries with the commits.
grounds: plugins/lane/README.md walkthrough runs changelog.

decisions.what: Who writes the script a subagent gives its result by?
decisions.decided: Lane: lay.py write puts the result script into the plugin with the check script. The developer AI writes no script for the order (O2), and the checks of the work's form it names come from its rules.
grounds: O2: "with no script of its own for the order"
.rn/20261013-rebuild/steering.md:76: "the script checking the work's form"; "Lane stays laid into each plugin whole"

decisions.what: Who takes part, and of what kind?
decisions.decided: developer AI (AI), which also runs changelog to try it; lay.py (script); check script (script), which lay.py puts into changelog; result script (script), which lay.py also puts into changelog; lead, writer and reviewer (AI). No step waits for a person.
grounds: plugins/lane/README.md: "Lane puts its checks into your plugin as one script, the check script"

decisions.what: What does the document show of Lane, and what does it leave to the architecture?
decisions.decided: Only what the developer AI runs, sees and receives, and what its subagents run and are told: lay.py's commands and what they show, the check script as one participant that lets calls through and tells the next start, and the result script as one a subagent runs. No hook event, file inside Lane or Claude Code mechanism.
grounds: plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json Q7: "the document says only what users mean to do, see and receive"

decisions.what: How is a line that a subagent is told, or that lay.py shows, given?
decisions.decided: As its exact text, a line told headed by the plugin's name, so that a developer reads what the developer AI and its subagents read, and a change to the text shows as a change to the UX.
grounds: plugins/lane/hooks/lane/hook.py heads each line a check tells with the plugin's name.

decisions.decided: "O1: The developer AI holds writer to two rules" and "O2: The developer AI has lead start writer and reviewer as its routes say".
grounds: plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json Q5 step 1: "its objective's ID and a short active verb phrase, the user its subject"

decisions.decided: Two rules on writer: on step 2, run only `git log --oneline`; on step 3, write only `CHANGELOG.md`. lay.py print shows both steps as they will read; once the developer AI approves, lay.py write writes them and puts the check script into changelog. Asked for an entry and a commit, writer runs git log and writes CHANGELOG.md, the check script lets both through, and writer ends with CHANGELOG.md written and no commit. No stop is drawn.
grounds: .rn/20261013-rebuild/steering.md:76: "a role's Bash runs only the commands its plugin declares for it, matched whole", so a rule names what may run, not what may not.
plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json Q5: the main path, the one most users take.

decisions.what: Does O2's main path run its subagents in the foreground or in the background?
decisions.decided: In the foreground, where each start comes back once its subagent has ended. The background path is left off the main path.
grounds: dev/lane/trials/trying.py runs Claude Code as `claude -p`, where subagents run in the foreground.

decisions.decided: The developer AI gives lay.py print the routes: lead starts writer; writer ends with `written`, then reviewer; reviewer with `more`, back to writer; reviewer with `good`, the end. It sees the routes and the steps they add to; once it approves, lay.py write writes them and puts the check script and the result script into changelog. Asked to update CHANGELOG.md for the next release, lead is told each start, with no stop: "changelog: Start `changelog:writer`."; writer gives `written` by the result script; "changelog: writer gave `written`. Start `changelog:reviewer`."; reviewer gives `more` or `good`; "changelog: reviewer gave `more`. Start `changelog:writer`." in a loop, and "changelog: reviewer gave `good`. Start no more subagents." at the end. lead ends with the reviewed entries.
grounds: .rn/20261013-rebuild/steering.md:76: routing "takes each role's result, tells the next and stops any other start"

decisions.what: Which plugins may the document name?
decisions.decided: Lane and the example plugin changelog only; no line names turn, rn or another plugin of the marketplace.
